difficultyRationale: A common, very practical early-career bug — knowing where @SpringBootApplication's implicit component scan actually looks.
prompt: A Spring Boot application has its main class, annotated `@SpringBootApplication`, at `com.example.orders.OrdersApplication`. A `@Service` class is defined at `com.example.billing.InvoiceService` — a sibling package, not a sub-package of `com.example.orders`. At startup, autowiring a dependency of type `InvoiceService` elsewhere fails with `NoSuchBeanDefinitionException`. Why isn't `InvoiceService` being found?
explanation: `@SpringBootApplication` includes `@ComponentScan` with no explicit `basePackages`, which defaults to scanning the package of the annotated class and all of its sub-packages. `com.example.billing` is not a sub-package of `com.example.orders` (they are siblings under `com.example`), so it falls outside the default scan and `InvoiceService` is never registered as a bean, regardless of it being correctly annotated `@Service`.

options.text: `@Service` only registers a bean when the annotated class sits in the exact same package as the main `@SpringBootApplication` class, and never when it's placed in any sub-package beneath it.
options.explanation: The default component scan does cover sub-packages of the main class's package, not just the exact same package; the problem here is that `com.example.billing` isn't a sub-package of `com.example.orders` at all.

options.text: The default component scan from `@SpringBootApplication` covers the main class's package and sub-packages; `com.example.billing` is a sibling, not a sub-package, so it falls outside that scan.
options.explanation: Correct. This is the classic package-structure pitfall: the implicit `@ComponentScan` only reaches down from the main class's package, never sideways to sibling packages, no matter how correctly the class elsewhere is annotated.

options.text: `@Service` beans always require an explicit `@Bean` method declared in some `@Configuration` class in addition to the stereotype annotation; the annotation alone never actually registers a bean by itself.
options.explanation: `@Service` (like `@Component`, `@Repository`, `@Controller`) is a stereotype annotation that component scanning picks up directly — no separate `@Bean` method is required, as long as the class is within a scanned package.

options.text: Spring Boot only scans the packages explicitly listed in `application.properties` under a `spring.main.sources` property, and this project simply hasn't configured that property with the right package names.
options.explanation: There is no such property governing component scan base packages; the scan base is determined by the location of the `@SpringBootApplication`-annotated class (or an explicit `@ComponentScan(basePackages = ...)`), not by an `application.properties` entry.

references.title: Spring Framework Javadoc — @ComponentScan ("If specific packages are not defined, scanning will occur recursively beginning with the package of the class that declares this annotation")
Spring Boot Reference Documentation — Structuring Your Code (locating the main application class as the root of the implicit scan)
